acv.quote: Two hundred and fifty K ACV.

data.reason: Halima, the COO, picked the rival because they named who would pick up on on-sale day. Our support tiers sounded like 'a queue with a faster timer.' Jordan thought the load test had won it.

trigger.action: Lead with what happens when payments fail mid on-sale.
trigger.why: Payments failed four minutes into a Friday on-sale. The old provider replied to a ticket after it ended.
trigger.quote: payments started failing about four minutes in

decider.action: Write for the COO who owns on-sale day, not the CTO.
decider.why: Ben, the CTO, wanted us. Halima decided in one meeting and only said 'good' to the load test.
decider.quote: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.

competitor.action: Say who covers a big on-sale, not just throughput and bots.
competitor.why: Ben said the rival brought named people. Afterward, Tixhaven's questions moved from throughput to names.
competitor.quote: Before that meeting it was throughput, queueing, bots. After, it was names.

message.action: Change support tiers and response times into named people who answer.
message.why: When Halima asked 'who's my person,' Jordan explained tiers and response times. She dismissed it.
message.quote: so it's a queue with a faster timer.

proof.action: Add a written on-sale morning plan showing who watches and who answers.
proof.why: Halima asked to see on paper what we do at minute four. We had nothing to show.
proof.quote: She wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning.

words.action: Say 'what happens when it's down' instead of uptime or support.
words.why: Halima brushed off uptime. Jordan noted that nobody at Tixhaven used the word 'support'.
words.quote: I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.
